| `symbol.type`                                             | string                | Resolved package-variable type; see [variable types](#resolved-variable-types). |
| `symbol.metrics.param_count`, `symbol.metrics.body_lines` | integer               | Callable measures; see [metrics](#stored-metrics).                              |
| `symbol.metrics.<name>`                                   | integer               | A [producer metric](#producer-metrics) declared by a selected kind.             |
| `path`, `package`, `module`, `snapshot`                   | string                | Witness source path, package, root key, and snapshot ID.                        |
| `line`, `column`                                          | number                | One-based witness line and UTF-16 column when positioned.                       |
| `role`                                                    | string                | Recorded occurrence role or native relationship name.                           |
| `dispatch`                                                | boolean               | Whether a witness was reached through known interface dispatch.                 |
| `depth`                                                   | number                | Recorded traversal hop distance.                                                |
| `relationship.kind`, `relationship.resolution`            | string                | Native kind and `static`, `dynamic`, `ambiguous`, or `unresolved` resolution.   |
| `relationship.props`, `relationship.props.<field>`        | object or schema type | Native relationship properties, when present.                                   |

Symbol `SELECT *` includes the symbol, its identity/name/ownership/property fields, witness fields, and relationship fields. It does not automatically include variable types or metrics; request them explicitly. Missing optional facts are `NULL`; unavailable required type/metric capabilities fail as described below.

File sources have a separate field set: `path`, `module`, `package`, `snapshot`, `file.lines`, `file.definitions`, `file.functions`, `file.structs`, and `file.build_constraint`. Their wildcard includes the first eight fields, omitting `file.build_constraint`. Symbol sources do not expose file metrics, and file sources do not expose `symbol` fields.

A source alias on a symbol source abbreviates **properties**: `FROM http.route:* AS r` makes `r.method` mean `symbol.props.method`, not `symbol.method`. Continue to write `symbol.name` for the symbol name. A file alias supports both site fields (`f.path`) and file fields (`f.lines`, `f.functions`, `f.build_constraint`). Alias names must match exactly.

### Predicates and globs

| Form                            | Example predicate                          | Behavior                                                           |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` | `symbol.metrics.param_count >= 4`          | Compares a scalar field with a type-compatible literal.            |
| `symbol IN selector`            | `symbol IN pkg:example.org/service:api/**` | Retains the projected canonical identities selected on the right.  |
| `symbol NOT IN selector`        | `symbol NOT IN method:Store.*`             | Excludes those projected identities.                               |
| `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL`        | `relationship.kind IS NOT NULL`            | Tests absence/presence explicitly.                                 |
| `MATCH`, `NOT MATCH`            | `path MATCH 'internal/**'`                 | Anchored, case-sensitive glob matching on a string field.          |
| `IMATCH`, `NOT IMATCH`          | `symbol.name IMATCH '*save*'`              | Anchored glob matching with Unicode simple case folding.           |
| `REQUIRES`, `NOT REQUIRES`      | `file.build_constraint REQUIRES 'hack'`    | Exact Boolean analysis of a modern Go header; file sources only.   |
| `NOT`, `AND`, `OR`, parentheses | `NOT (role = 'write' OR line IS NULL)`     | Combines predicates, with precedence `NOT`, then `AND`, then `OR`. |

Comparisons take literal values on the right, not another field. `IN` accepts a selector, not a literal list, and its left operand must be `symbol`. Objects, arrays, and the whole `symbol` object cannot be scalar-compared or ordered; project a typed scalar property instead. An unknown property or one whose selected schemas disagree about its type fails binding.

`NULL` follows three-valued logic: a comparison or match with a missing value is unknown, `NOT unknown` is unknown, and `WHERE` retains only true rows. Use `IS NULL`, rather than `= NULL`, to find missing values. For example, retain routes with an absent description or a nonempty POST description:

```sql
SELECT symbol.name, r.description
FROM http.route:* AS r
WHERE r.description IS NULL OR (r.method = 'POST' AND r.description != '')
```

Globs are anchored to the whole string. `*` matches within one slash segment, `?` matches one character, `**` matches whole segments, `/...` abbreviates `/**`, and backslashes escape glob characters. Thus `'*save*'` is a name substring search, `'internal/*'` covers one directory level, and `'internal/**'` covers descendants. `%` and `_` are not SQL wildcards. `IMATCH` uses simple case folding, so it does not expand `ß` into `ss`. Selector patterns remain case sensitive, and matching never changes canonical identity.

## Functions and bounds

| Function          | Result and options                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `files()`         | Non-excluded indexed files, including files with zero definitions. Standalone source; `include_excluded => TRUE` also includes build-excluded snapshot members. |
| `definitions(s)`  | Declaration witnesses, projecting the declared symbol. No options.                                                                                              |
| `callers(s)`      | Incoming witnesses to callables, projecting the enclosing caller; `depth` defaults to 1.                                                                        |
| `callees(s)`      | Outgoing call witnesses, projecting the callee; `depth` defaults to 1.                                                                                          |
| `references(s)`   | All recorded non-definition uses, projecting the referenced symbol. No options.                                                                                 |
| `reads(s)`        | Recorded read uses, projecting the referenced symbol. No options.                                                                                               |
| `writes(s)`       | Recorded write uses, projecting the written symbol. No options.                                                                                                 |
| `methods(s)`      | Owned method declarations, projecting each method. No options.                                                                                                  |
| `implementers(s)` | Recorded types implementing the selected interfaces. No options.                                                                                                |
| `inheritors(s)`   | Direct struct/interface embedding declarations. No options.                                                                                                     |
| `incoming(s)`     | Native witnesses, projecting each relationship's source; optional `via`.                                                                                        |
| `outgoing(s)`     | Native witnesses, projecting each relationship's target; optional `via`.                                                                                        |
| `traverse(s)`     | Reachable symbols with minimum hop distances; `direction` defaults to `outgoing`, `depth` to 3, optional `via`.                                                 |
| `path(a, b)`      | One shortest recorded path; `depth` defaults to 8, optional `via`.                                                                                              |
| `graph(s)`        | Nodes, native kinds, sites, properties, and omissions; `direction` defaults to `both`, `depth` to 2, `nodes` to 150; optional `via`, `exclude`, or `access`.    |

Nested functions consume their inner source's canonical symbol projection, not its printed strings. For example, `callers(callees(func:Entry))` finds callers of the functions `Entry` calls. `references`, `reads`, and `writes` with a direct selector also match referenced dependency identities without a local declaration; a bare selector normally selects declarations. `files()` is standalone and cannot feed symbol navigation. There is no SQL `uses()` function; the compact language's `:uses` relation is documented separately.

Depth-one `callees` reports the declared call target, including an interface method. Multi-hop callee traversal (`depth > 1`), `traverse`, and call paths expand known interface implementations; those implementation witnesses carry `dispatch = TRUE`. Callers of a concrete method can also include recorded interface-dispatch sites. These facts describe possible targets in the selected snapshots, not a guarantee of runtime execution.

Source arguments precede named options, which use `=>`. Each option may appear once and only on a function listing it above. For example, `callers(func:Save, depth => 2)` is valid; `callers(depth => 2, func:Save)` and `reads(field:Total, depth => 2)` fail.

| Option             | Allowed values and defaults                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `depth`            | Integer 1–8. Defaults: callers/callees 1, traverse 3, path 8, graph 2.                                                                                                      |
| `nodes`            | Graph-only integer 1–1,000; default 150. Bounds nodes, not SQL rows.                                                                                                        |
| `direction`        | Traverse: `'incoming'` or `'outgoing'` (default). Graph also accepts `'both'` (default), unioning independent directional walks.                                            |
| `via`              | Nonempty comma-separated string of exact registered native relationship names. No wildcard expansion.                                                                       |
| `exclude`          | Graph-only comma-separated package patterns/keywords; default `'std,builtin,gorm.io/...'`. `'none'` disables exclusions. See [graph exclusions](/graph#excluding-packages). |
| `access`           | Graph-only comma-separated `'call'`, `'read'`, `'write'` selections. Omission uses calls. Mutually exclusive with `via`.                                                    |
| `include_excluded` | Files-only `TRUE` or `FALSE` (default); includes snapshot members excluded by build selection.                                                                              |

Without `via`, traversal and paths follow calls and known dispatch. With `via`, they follow only the selected native kinds. `incoming`/`outgoing` always use native relationships; omitting `via` there admits all recorded native kinds. Empty list items, unknown relationships, unsupported options, and out-of-range bounds fail explicitly. Traversal fails beyond 10,000 symbols; graph bounds report omissions.

Paths and graphs are terminal sources: use `SELECT *` without `WHERE`, `ORDER BY`, or SQL `LIMIT`, and do not nest them in other functions. Control a graph with `depth`, `nodes`, and `exclude`. A path follows the source-to-target direction and returns one shortest recorded path; no path means `total: 0` with no `path`. Graphs return nodes, edges, sites, and omission metadata; inspect candidates when a call-graph source is ambiguous.

Traversal describes recorded possible reachability. It does not guarantee execution. Ambiguous candidates and unresolved references remain visible without inferred links between similar names.

## Resolved variable types

`symbol.type` is the resolved type of a package-level variable, available in projection, predicates and ordering. For example:

```sql
SELECT symbol.name, path, line, symbol.type
FROM var:*
WHERE symbol.type = 'context.Context' OR symbol.type = '*gorm.io/gorm.DB'
```

Types use canonical import paths and preserve pointers/composites. Import aliases and type aliases resolve to their targets; distinct named types keep their identity. Local variables and fields are outside this initial type field; non-variable symbols return `NULL`. Request the field explicitly; `SELECT *` is unchanged. Types come from immutable document declarations in format 8, never from current source files. Queries requesting types require complete typed coverage and fail before filtering if a variable's type was not recorded; reindex or republish with type facts. Historical snapshots retain their original availability. External producers may supply a nonempty `declared_type` string on a proven `var` declaration in format 8. Metric-only queries retain their document-free path; type queries use the existing decoded document cache.

## Content generations

`symbol.generation` (integer) counts the distinct implementations a symbol has had along the base chain of the snapshot that declares it: 1 where the chain first defines it, plus one at every later snapshot whose `content_fp` differs. A signature-only change (a parameter rename), a comment-only edit and a move between files keep it; a re-add after a delete continues the count. It is read from `symbol_deltas` without decoding documents, and symbols no selected snapshot declares, such as standard library callees, read `NULL`. Request it explicitly; `SELECT *` is unchanged.

```sql
SELECT symbol.name, path, symbol.generation FROM func:* WHERE symbol.generation > 10 ORDER BY symbol.generation DESC
```

`uir history symbol <selector>` lists the snapshots, with their commits, at which one symbol's generation advanced. The selector must match exactly one declaration in the current checkout. Generations follow publication order: a historical import published on top of a newer head counts in import order, not commit order.

## Effects and determinism

`symbol.effects` (string) lists, sorted and comma-separated, the external effects of a function, method or package-level variable through everything it calls, references as a function value, or reads or writes as a package-level variable, however deep: `time.read`, `random.read`, `env.read`, `env.write`, `process.read`, `process.write`, `file.read`, `file.write`, `network.io`, `db.read`, `db.write`, `global.read` (a package-level variable indexed code writes), `global.write`, `goroutine`, `channel`, `lock.read`, `lock.write`, `map.order` and `unknown`. `symbol.deterministic` (boolean) is true when none applies other than the lock and `map.order` effects. Library calls are classified by the catalog in `effects/catalog.go`; Methods a catalogued library calls back on the values passed to it (`String` and `Error` for `fmt`, `MarshalJSON` for `encoding/json` including nested fields, `Less` for `sort`, and so on) count as calls. `unknown` is a call through an interface, a function value or a type parameter, a value of interface type or a function value passed to a catalogued library, a function without a body (linkname or assembly), an uncatalogued library function, an unresolved call, or a document indexed before format 12, so determinism is never over-claimed. `time.Date`, `time.Unix` and `time.Parse` are `env.read`, whatever zone they are given. Any file read counts, including files tracked in the repository. Other symbols read `NULL`. Request the fields explicitly; `SELECT *` is unchanged. `uir effects <selector>` reports one symbol's effects with the shortest path to each.

```sql
SELECT symbol.query_name FROM func:* WHERE symbol.deterministic = TRUE
```

## Build constraints

Inspect the explicit modern Go build constraint, including files excluded from the indexed build:

```sh
uir query "SELECT path, file.build_constraint FROM files(include_excluded => TRUE) WHERE path MATCH '**/hack/**/*.go' AND file.build_constraint NOT REQUIRES 'hack' ORDER BY path"
```

`include_excluded` accepts `TRUE` or `FALSE` and defaults to false. The option exposes source revisions and excluded documents already in the selected snapshot. Gitignore, module scope and test-file discovery still apply. Excluded documents have no extracted symbols; their zero `file.definitions` is an extraction count. The option does not type-check excluded code.

`file.build_constraint` is a string containing the normalized expression without `//go:build`. A Go source without a recognized modern header returns an empty string; a non-Go source returns `NULL`. File aliases support `f.build_constraint`. Request the field explicitly: the file wildcard's eight columns do not include it.

`REQUIRES 'hack'` accepts a single case-sensitive positive Go tag and performs exact Boolean analysis. The expression must be satisfiable and impossible to satisfy without the tag. `hack`, `hack && linux`, and `(hack || linux) && !linux` require `hack`; `ignore`, `!hack`, `hack || linux`, and `hack && !hack` do not. Tags are Boolean variables independent of the host environment. Filename suffixes and legacy-only `// +build` directives do not satisfy this explicit modern-header rule. `NOT REQUIRES` negates the result; non-Go `NULL` remains unknown under either operator.

The field reads hash-verified source bytes belonging to the immutable snapshot through the existing checkout/stored-blob/pinned-Git recovery path. No schema migration or reindex is required when those bytes remain available. Unavailable or corrupt source bytes and malformed or duplicate recognized directives are execution errors with source and snapshot context. Exact analysis fails explicitly beyond 65,536 decision nodes or on cancellation.

Ordinary file and metric queries perform no additional source reads. Constraint queries recover source bytes on cache misses and reuse a bounded, per-pipeline cache of parsed headers keyed by content hash. Cold queries can read all selected Go source candidates before WHERE filtering; LIMIT limits returned rows, not this work. Querying historical snapshots never silently substitutes current checkout content.

## Stored metrics

Find small files with few definitions, or callables with many parameters or long bodies:

```sh
uir query 'SELECT path, file.lines, file.definitions FROM files() WHERE file.lines < 100 AND file.definitions < 3 ORDER BY path LIMIT 1000'
uir query 'SELECT symbol.name, path, line, symbol.metrics.param_count, symbol.metrics.body_lines FROM func:* WHERE symbol.metrics.param_count > 3 OR symbol.metrics.body_lines > 50 ORDER BY path, line'
```

| Field                        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `file.lines`                 | Physical source lines, including blanks and comments. Empty content has zero lines; a terminating newline adds no extra line; CRLF counts once.                                    |
| `file.definitions`           | The active document's indexed declaration count, including fields, package variables and constants, excluding references and function-local bindings.                              |
| `file.functions`             | Number of declared functions and concrete methods; excludes interface signatures, function literals and function-valued variables.                                                 |
| `file.structs`               | Number of declared struct types; excludes fields, interfaces and type aliases.                                                                                                     |
| `symbol.metrics.param_count` | Value parameters, expanding grouped names and counting a variadic parameter once. Receivers and type parameters do not count.                                                      |
| `symbol.metrics.body_lines`  | Inclusive physical span of the body's delimiters. Documentation and signature-only lines do not count. A one-line body counts as one; a declaration without a body returns `NULL`. |

All six metric/count fields above have catalog type `integer`. `files()` also exposes `path`, `module`, `package`, and `snapshot`; its `SELECT *` projects those four site fields and all four file counts. `FROM files() AS f` supports `f.path`, `f.lines`, `f.definitions`, `f.functions`, and `f.structs`. Symbol navigation cannot consume a file source. Symbol `SELECT *` retains its existing fields; request callable metrics explicitly. Standard root, location, snapshot and limit options apply. Test files participate when the snapshot indexed them. Existing coverage warnings describe syntax/partial extraction.

Source line counts and callable metrics are recorded during indexing/publication, with immutable source revisions and document membership deciding which values a snapshot serves. `file.definitions` reads the active document header; `file.functions` and `file.structs` count declarations from decoded active documents. The line/definition and callable-metric examples above read neither source bytes nor full document JSON. Navigation and requested symbol properties can require document content. Filtering and ordering still inspect matching candidates before limiting; `LIMIT` caps returned rows rather than scanning work.

Existing snapshots remain readable. Metrics are not backfilled during migration or query execution. When a requested metric was not recorded, the query fails with its snapshot/path/declaration and reindex or republish guidance; it never substitutes zero. Reindexing a historical revision provides a metric-bearing snapshot while leaving earlier documents intact. Ordinary SQL `NULL` rules apply to a known bodyless declaration and to metric fields on non-callable symbols.

External producers may include `metrics` on a callable `DocumentSymbol` in document format 7:

```json
{"version": 1, "param_count": 2, "body_lines": 4}
```

Here `version` is the metric semantics version, `param_count` is nonnegative, and `body_lines` is positive or `null` for a declaration without a body. Omit the entire metric record when it is unavailable; queries requesting it then fail with republish guidance. File lines are derived from the publication's verified source. Go indexing records function/method parameters and body spans, including bodyless interface signatures. Metrics do not change canonical symbol identities or semantic fingerprints.

Run the focused and repository acceptance checks with `gavel fixtures fixtures/queryable-metrics.md`. Real-corpus benchmark instructions are in [the metric plan](https://github.com/flanksource/uir/blob/main/docs/queryable-metrics-plan.md).

## Producer metrics

A non-Go producer can publish its own per-symbol integer metrics and query them beside the callable ones. A kind declares its metrics in the publication's `kinds`, by name with a description:

```json
{"name": "acme.rule", "category": "callable", "metrics": {
  "variables": {"description": "Variables the rule declares"},
  "fan_in": {"description": "Distinct rules that call this rule"}
}}
```

Every declaration of that kind then records a value for each declared metric in its document symbol's `measures`, which requires document format 10:

```json
{"key": "…", "kind": "acme.rule", "measures": {"variables": 14, "fan_in": 2}, "…": "…"}
```

Publication refuses, before writing anything, a metric name that is not a lower snake_case identifier or that is `param_count` or `body_lines`; `measures` in a document older than format 10 or on a declaration without a canonical `id`; a negative value; a name the symbol's kind does not declare; and a symbol missing a value for one its kind declares. A kind that declares no metrics carries no `measures`. Each error names the kind and the symbol, and the metric at fault. Values are stored in `declaration_measures` by document ordinal, declaration key and name (migration [`22_producer_metrics.hcl`](https://github.com/flanksource/uir/blob/main/storage/migrations/22_producer_metrics.hcl)), and the declared metrics in `symbol_kind_metrics`.

`symbol.metrics.<name>` is a catalogued `integer` field whenever a kind the source selects declares it, the same way a declared property types `symbol.props.<name>`. It works in projection, `WHERE` and `ORDER BY`, on symbol sources and on navigation rows such as `callers`, `callees` and `traverse`, for kinds of any category:

```sh
uir query 'SELECT symbol.name, symbol.metrics.variables, symbol.metrics.fan_in FROM acme.rule:* WHERE symbol.metrics.variables > 10 AND symbol.metrics.fan_in >= 2 ORDER BY symbol.metrics.variables DESC'
```

A metric no selected kind declares is an unknown field. A row whose kind does not declare a requested metric reads `NULL`. A declaration whose kind declares the metric but whose document recorded no value, such as one published before the kind declared it, fails the query with its snapshot, path, declaration, kind and metric, and asks to republish; it never reads as zero or `NULL`. Like the callable metrics, a metric-only query reads the stored values without decoding documents.

Metrics evolve additively. Publishing a kind again may declare new metrics, after which every new document of the kind must record them; removing a declared metric or changing its description is refused, naming the kind and the metric. To change a metric's meaning, declare a new name. Format 9 documents remain readable; only their producer metric fields are unavailable.

## Runnable domain publication

From the repository root, build the CLI and generate a publication containing HTTP → handler → topic → consumer links plus parallel Kubernetes relationships:

```sh
make build
mkdir -p .tmp
go run -tags hack ./hack/sql-domains > .tmp/sql-domains.json
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-example.db import .tmp/sql-domains.json
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-example.db query "SELECT r.method, r.path, r.description FROM http.route:* AS r WHERE r.path IMATCH '/orders/**'"
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-example.db query "SELECT * FROM path(http.route:Orders, messaging.consumer:Consume, via => 'http.handled_by,messaging.publishes_to,messaging.delivers_to')" --format json
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-example.db query "SELECT * FROM graph(k8s.service:checkout, via => 'k8s.selects,k8s.uses_config', direction => 'outgoing')" --format json
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-example.db serve --host localhost --port 8080
```

The generator in [`hack/sql-domains/main.go`](https://github.com/flanksource/uir/blob/main/hack/sql-domains/main.go) is a complete producer example. `kinds` registers each custom name, handle category, and optional object JSON Schema. `relationships` registers namespaced native names, coarse UIR types, and optional property schemas. Immutable declarations store queryable `props` and preserve the producer's full `payload`. Schemas are immutable for a registered name and use local references; use a new kind name to change its schema.

Document format 4 adds `relationships`: source canonical ID, target IDs or reference, native kind, typed properties, resolution (`static`, `dynamic`, `ambiguous`, or `unresolved`), and source range/byte/text evidence. Publication validates schemas and all identities before updating the head. Source and target postings use the existing posting index; relationship details stay in snapshot-selected documents. Include distinguishing tenant, service, broker, cluster, or namespace context in canonical identities' module, package, and owner fields.

Concrete HTTP, messaging, and Kubernetes extractors are separate producers. This implementation consumes their explicit links. Older snapshots still answer queries over their existing facts; native navigation on documents before format 4 fails with reindex/reimport guidance.

## API and browser

`POST /api/v1/modules/query` accepts `args: [expression]`, `language: auto|compact|sql`, and existing root, location, snapshot, and limit options. Row responses add `columns` and `rows` beside the existing `matches`, `symbols`, `coverage`, and `stages`; paths use `path`, and graphs use `graph`. Native graph sites carry their own snapshot and source location so evidence opens the correct file.

For a server using the cookbook's Go database:

```sh
curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/api/v1/modules/query -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"args":["SELECT symbol.name AS caller FROM callers(func:Run) ORDER BY caller LIMIT 1"],"language":"sql","root":"example.org/service"}'
```

The relevant response fields below show why `total` differs from the returned row count: both `Entry` and `Replay` match, but the SQL limit admits one row. Column descriptors preserve the output name, bound field, and catalog type:

```json
{
  "columns": [{"name": "caller", "field": "symbol.name", "type": "string"}],
  "rows": [{"caller": "Entry"}],
  "total": 2
}
```

SQL CLI JSON and YAML retain this result envelope, including pre-limit totals and source witnesses. Human-readable output renders projected values, paths, or graphs. Compact CLI JSON retains its existing row format.

`GET /api/v1/modules/query-catalog` supplies functions, registered kinds, fields, and property schemas for completion. `GET /api/v1/modules/suggest-selectors?...&language=sql` completes registered selector prefixes. The Query page persists language in its URL, renders projected columns, paths, and graphs, and opens witnesses in Source. The Query page and Cmd+K share SQL completion and positioned diagnostics. Ctrl/Cmd+Space requests suggestions; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter runs the query.

Run the executable verification fixture with `gavel fixtures fixtures/sql-query.md`. It checks parser and query behavior, API integration, frontend models, and the runnable CLI publication.

## Errors and unsupported SQL

Syntax and binding errors report a message, source line/column when available, and a hint. Queries are bounded to 65,536 bytes, 64 nested parentheses, and 64 `NOT` tokens. Correct the query rather than switching database dialect: this grammar is the same on both storage backends. Missing required stored facts ask for reindexing or republishing; historical snapshots do not gain new capabilities in place. Partial/syntax coverage and missing heads remain evidence gaps, not proof that a symbol has no uses.

UIR SQL does not implement joins, SQL subqueries, CTEs, aggregation (`COUNT`, `SUM`, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`), `DISTINCT`, `UNION`, `OFFSET`, arithmetic, scalar function calls, field-to-field comparisons, literal-list `IN`, `LIKE`, `<>`, or writes. Use nested navigation instead of joins, `MATCH`/`IMATCH` instead of `LIKE`, and `!=` instead of `<>`. A graph or path query cannot have row clauses. The [cookbook](/sql-examples) includes valid alternatives.

The implementation sources are [`sqlsyntax/ast.go`](https://github.com/flanksource/uir/blob/main/query/sqlsyntax/ast.go) and [`sqlsyntax/parser.go`](https://github.com/flanksource/uir/blob/main/query/sqlsyntax/parser.go) for syntax, [`sql_bind.go`](https://github.com/flanksource/uir/blob/main/query/sql_bind.go) for functions/options/selectors, and [`sql_rows.go`](https://github.com/flanksource/uir/blob/main/query/sql_rows.go) and [`sql_files.go`](https://github.com/flanksource/uir/blob/main/query/sql_files.go) for fields and projection. `go test ./query -run TestQuery -ginkgo.focus='SQL documentation examples'` parses every SQL fence in this reference and the cookbook and checks that every registered source function has an example.

# UIR Model Reference

This document is the canonical model reference for the Universal Intermediate Representation (UIR) used in this repository.

It is written for two audiences:

* plugin and extractor authors that need to generate valid UIR
* consumers that need to read or transform emitted UIR JSON

`uir-api.md` covers broader architectural and conceptual material. This document stays close to the current implementation in the root `uir` package, the current JSON shape, and the current plugin transport layer.

## Scope and source of truth

* The Go types in the root `uir` package (`github.com/flanksource/uir`) are the canonical model.
* The JSON field names on those types are the canonical serialized field names.
* The registered concrete node variants are the entries in `Nodes`.
* The registered concrete statement variants are the entries in `Statements`.
* When this document and the code disagree, the code wins.

## Serialization contract

### Root vs node documents

* `UIR` is the root aggregate. It carries neither `node_kind` nor `node_type`.
* An interface-typed slot holds its value under its kind: `{"$<kind>": <value>}` (`uir.SlotKey`). The slots are every block child (`BlockStmt.children`), every element of the flat node array (`MarshalNodes` / `UnmarshalJSON`), and the `Node`-typed statement and relationship fields (`MethodCallStmt.Method`, `DispatchCallStmt.Method` / `candidates`, `EndpointCallStmt.endpoint`, `RecordReadStmt.Record`, `RecordWriteStmt.Record`, `UIRRelationship.from` / `to`). Because the kind precedes the value, `uir.Unmarshal` (and every `UnmarshalJSON`, which delegates to it) decodes in one pass over the document without buffering a subtree to find its discriminator. A slot is a single key; an unknown kind, or a slot holding two kinds, is refused. A slot whose first key does not start with `$` is the legacy inline layout — the value itself, stamped with its discriminator, as the Python and Java producers and documents written before the tagged layout carry it — and still decodes. `UIR.ToMap` / `AssertionEnv` (and `uir.UnwrapSlots`) present every slot inline, so assertions see one shape whichever layout a document uses.
* `node_kind` is the node discriminator. It is the kind the node's concrete Go type is registered under in `NodeMarshaler`: the node's static `GetType()` (`package`, `class`, `method`, `record_field`, …) for every registered node, and `ref` for a `NodeRef`. It names a `Node` slot (`{"$ref": …}`) and is stamped inside the slot's value too. A node nested through a concrete field (`UIR.packages`, `TypedNode.methods`, …) carries no `node_kind`, because its Go type is already known. Decoding a `Node` slot without a kind, or with one nothing is registered under, is an error rather than a guess.
* `node_type` is `Identifier` data, not a discriminator. A `MethodNode` may carry `node_type: "constructor"`, and a `NodeRef` carries the `node_type` of the node it points at, so `{"node_kind": "ref", "node_type": "method", "method": "GetUser"}` decodes as a reference to a method, never as a `MethodNode`. Stamping the concrete kind over `node_type` would change the node's identity, which is why the discriminator has a key of its own.
* Concrete statements are identified by `statement_type`, which the codec stamps from the concrete type's registered kind rather than from the embedded `Type` field.
* A statement whose `Type` is refined past its registered kind keeps `statement_type` at the kind and carries the refined value in `statement_refinement`, e.g. `{"statement_type": "call", "statement_refinement": "call:package"}`. In a block child the slot key already names the kind, so the value carries its own `Type` instead: `{"$call": {"statement_type": "call:package", …}}`. A refinement is accepted when its longest registered `:`-prefix is the statement's own kind, or when the kind lists it explicitly (a `control:block` may be refined to `doc`); anything else is refused on encode and decode.
* `MethodNode.body` is always a `BlockStmt`, even when the body object omits `statement_type` in current Go builder output.

### Shared embedding model

Most concrete nodes embed the same three building blocks:

* `Metadata`
* `Identifier`
* `SourceCode`

That means most node objects can carry:

* annotations, comments, and arbitrary properties
* `module`, `package`, `type`, `method`, `field`, `signature`, and `node_type`
* a `sourceCode` object

### Empty-object behavior

The Go model uses value types for several nested objects. In practice this means some fields often serialize as empty objects instead of being omitted, for example:

* `sourceCode: {}`
* `validation: {}`
* `input: {}`
* `output: {}`

Consumers should treat those empty objects as "present but empty", not as meaningful data.

### Current Go JSON quirks

These are part of the current emitted surface and consumers should tolerate them:

* `MethodCallStmt` marshals its target node under `Method`, not `method`.
* `RecordReadStmt` and `RecordWriteStmt` marshal their target node under `Record`, not `record`.
* `TypedNode` is registered as `node_kind: "class"` and defaults to `node_type: "class"`, not `"type"`.
* `UIR.functions` stores `MethodNode` values. In current Go output those nodes still use `node_type: "method"`, and a `MethodNode` crossing a `Node` slot is stamped `node_kind: "method"`.
* `SourceCode` in Go JSON inlines location fields under `sourceCode`; the proto transport nests them under `source_code.location`.

## Model map

### Canonical root shape

| Field       | Type             | Meaning                                                                                  |
| ----------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `modules`   | `[]ModuleNode`   | Top-level modules or namespaces.                                                         |
| `packages`  | `[]PackageNode`  | Top-level packages or schemas.                                                           |
| `types`     | `[]TypedNode`    | Top-level types not nested under packages.                                               |
| `records`   | `[]ASTRecord`    | Top-level records or schemas.                                                            |
| `tables`    | `[]RecordTable`  | Top-level relational tables and views. SQL extraction emits these rather than `records`. |
| `endpoints` | `[]ASTEndpoint`  | Top-level integration endpoints.                                                         |
| `functions` | `[]MethodNode`   | Top-level callable declarations.                                                         |
| `hierarchy` | `HierarchyGraph` | Optional non-AST structural graph.                                                       |
| `rawFiles`  | `[]RawFile`      | Verbatim files to emit alongside generated code.                                         |

### Canonical concrete node variants

These are the node kinds currently registered in `NodeMarshaler`, keyed by the `node_kind` a node carries across a `Node` slot. For every variant except `NodeRef` the kind equals the node's default `node_type`.

| `node_kind`    | Go type            | Typical role                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `module`       | `ModuleNode`       | Highest-level grouping such as module, namespace, package scope, or tenant.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `package`      | `PackageNode`      | Package, schema, namespace, folder-level logical grouping.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `class`        | `TypedNode`        | Class, interface-like type, struct, object type, or composite declaration.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `method`       | `MethodNode`       | Method or function declaration.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `record`       | `ASTRecord`        | Table-like or schema-like data shape.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `endpoint`     | `ASTEndpoint`      | External integration point such as HTTP, Kafka, JMS, SOAP, or gRPC endpoint.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `record_field` | `RecordField`      | Field within a record, method signature, type, or package variable list.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `table`        | `RecordTable`      | Relational table or view. Unlike `record` it keeps what a database catalogue reports: typed columns, an ordered primary key, indexes, and foreign keys. Project it with `AsRecord()` when a consumer only understands records. |
| `column`       | `RecordColumn`     | Column of a table, carrying the dialect's own SQL type alongside the portable `fieldType`, plus ordinal, nullability, primary-key and auto-increment as distinct facts.                                                        |
| `index`        | `RecordIndex`      | Index over a table's columns, in index order.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `foreign_key`  | `RecordForeignKey` | Referential constraint from one table's columns to another's.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ref`          | `NodeRef`          | Leaf reference to a node by its `Identifier`. Its `node_type` is the referenced node's type, so it round-trips as a reference instead of decoding as the node it names.                                                        |

### Canonical concrete statement variants

These are the statement kinds currently registered in `StatementMarshaler`. A statement is always stamped with one of these under `statement_type`; a finer `Type` travels under `statement_refinement`.

| `statement_type`         | Go type               | Role                                                                    |
| ------------------------ | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `assignment`             | `AssignmentStmt`      | Assignment or mutation.                                                 |
| `assignment:binary`      | `BinaryStmt`          | Binary expression.                                                      |
| `control:block`          | `BlockStmt`           | Statement block and scope.                                              |
| `control:break`          | `BreakStmt`           | Loop break.                                                             |
| `assignment:cast`        | `CastStmt`            | Type cast.                                                              |
| `control:condition`      | `ConditionStmt`       | Wrapped condition expression.                                           |
| `decl:const`             | `ConstDeclStmt`       | Constant declaration.                                                   |
| `control:continue`       | `ContinueStmt`        | Loop continue.                                                          |
| `call:api`               | `EndpointCallStmt`    | Endpoint invocation.                                                    |
| `assignment:expression`  | `ExprStmt`            | Expression wrapper.                                                     |
| `control:loop:for`       | `ForStmt`             | `for` loop.                                                             |
| `decl:func`              | `FunctionDeclStmt`    | Inline or nested function declaration.                                  |
| `control:if`             | `IfStmt`              | Conditional branch.                                                     |
| `assignment:literal`     | `LiteralStmt`         | Literal value.                                                          |
| `call`                   | `MethodCallStmt`      | Method or function invocation.                                          |
| `dispatch_call`          | `DispatchCallStmt`    | Invocation whose implementation is chosen at run time among candidates. |
| `call:read:record`       | `RecordReadStmt`      | Read from record-like source.                                           |
| `call:write:record`      | `RecordWriteStmt`     | Write to record-like source.                                            |
| `control:return`         | `ReturnStmt`          | Return statement.                                                       |
| `control:switch`         | `SwitchStmt`          | Switch or match.                                                        |
| `control:throw`          | `ThrowStmt`           | Throw or raise.                                                         |
| `control:try`            | `TryStmt`             | Try/catch.                                                              |
| `assignment:tuple`       | `TupleStmt`           | Tuple expression.                                                       |
| `decl:type`              | `TypeDeclStmt`        | Type declaration.                                                       |
| `assignment:unary`       | `UnaryStmt`           | Unary expression.                                                       |
| `decl:var`               | `VariableDeclStmt`    | Variable declaration.                                                   |
| `assignment:variable`    | `VariableStmt`        | Variable expression.                                                    |
| `control:loop:while`     | `WhileStmt`           | `while` loop.                                                           |
| `doc`                    | `DocStmt`             | Documentation node in executable trees.                                 |
| `test`                   | `TestStmt`            | Test block.                                                             |
| `raw`                    | `RawStmt`             | Lossless raw source fragment.                                           |
| `assignment:destructure` | `DestructuringStmt`   | Object or array destructuring.                                          |
| `assignment:template`    | `TemplateLiteralStmt` | Template or interpolated string.                                        |

## Shared primitives

### Identifier

`Identifier` is the logical name carrier for most nodes.

See [`docs/symbols.md`](/symbols) for rendered formats, durable identity scope, reference forms, and call-query examples.

| Field       | Type     | Meaning                                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`        | `string` | Optional explicit UUID-like identifier. Rarely needed for plugin authors.                                                  |
| `module`    | `string` | Top-level grouping. For endpoints this is often the base URL or service root.                                              |
| `package`   | `string` | Package, schema, namespace, or secondary grouping.                                                                         |
| `type`      | `string` | Type, class, table, topic family, or record name.                                                                          |
| `method`    | `string` | Method or function name.                                                                                                   |
| `field`     | `string` | Field or variable name.                                                                                                    |
| `signature` | `string` | Disambiguator for overloads or statement-local identity.                                                                   |
| `node_type` | `string` | The node's declared type (e.g. `method` or `constructor`). Identifier data, not the codec discriminator — see `node_kind`. |

Notes:

* UIR names are hierarchical, not generic. Most declarations do not have a standalone `name` field.
* Endpoint identifiers stringify with `/` separators instead of `.` and `:`.
* Producers should populate the deepest meaningful identifier components and leave unrelated ones empty.

### Location

| Field           | Type        | Meaning                          |
| --------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- |
| `path`          | `string`    | Source path or virtual path.     |
| `start_line`    | `int`       | First source line.               |
| `end_line`      | `int`       | Last source line.                |
| `column`        | `int`       | Optional source column.          |
| `last_modified` | `timestamp` | Optional last modification time. |

### SourceCode

In Go JSON, `Location` is inlined inside `sourceCode`.

| Field           | Type        | Meaning                                                            |
| --------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `path`          | `string`    | Source or virtual path.                                            |
| `start_line`    | `int`       | First source line.                                                 |
| `end_line`      | `int`       | Last source line.                                                  |
| `column`        | `int`       | Optional source column.                                            |
| `last_modified` | `timestamp` | Optional modification time.                                        |
| `content`       | `string`    | Optional source snippet.                                           |
| `language`      | `string`    | Language hint such as `go`, `xml`, `typescript`, `sql`, or `yaml`. |

### Metadata

| Field         | Type             | Meaning                               |
| ------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `annotations` | `[]Annotation`   | Structured annotations or decorators. |
| `comments`    | `[]Comment`      | Source comments or extracted docs.    |
| `properties`  | `map[string]any` | Unstructured extension data.          |

### Annotation

`Annotation` reuses `Identifier` and carries a single typed value or a named value map.

| Field             | Type                    | Meaning                               |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| identifier fields | `Identifier`            | Symbolic identity for the annotation. |
| `value`           | `TypedValue`            | Single annotation value.              |
| `values`          | `map[string]TypedValue` | Named annotation attributes.          |

### Comment

`Comment` inlines `Location`.

| Field           | Type          | Meaning                                    |
| --------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| location fields | `Location`    | Comment location.                          |
| `text`          | `string`      | Comment body.                              |
| `type`          | `CommentType` | Single-line, multi-line, or documentation. |
| `context`       | `string`      | Optional extraction context.               |

### TypedValue

Exactly one of these should normally be set.

| Field    | Type        | Meaning                |
| -------- | ----------- | ---------------------- |
| `string` | `string`    | String value.          |
| `float`  | `float64`   | Floating-point value.  |
| `int`    | `int64`     | Integer value.         |
| `bool`   | `bool`      | Boolean value.         |
| `date`   | `timestamp` | Timestamp value.       |
| `unit`   | `Unit`      | Structured unit value. |

### Unit

| Field   | Type       | Meaning                                                |
| ------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `type`  | `UnitType` | Unit family such as `currency`, `bytes`, or `seconds`. |
| `value` | `string`   | Optional modifier such as currency code or timezone.   |

### TypeReference

`TypeReference` is the main cross-language type carrier.

| Field             | Type              | Meaning                                                               |
| ----------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`            | `string`          | Base type name such as `string`, `Promise`, `User`, or `Map`.         |
| `fieldType`       | `RecordFieldType` | Primitive or schema-oriented fallback type.                           |
| `typeArgs`        | `[]TypeReference` | Generic arguments.                                                    |
| `union`           | `[]TypeReference` | Union members.                                                        |
| `intersection`    | `[]TypeReference` | Intersection members.                                                 |
| `optional`        | `bool`            | Optional or nullable marker.                                          |
| `literalValue`    | `string`          | Literal type payload.                                                 |
| `isArray`         | `bool`            | Array marker.                                                         |
| `tupleElements`   | `[]TypeReference` | Tuple element types.                                                  |
| `functionParams`  | `[]TypeReference` | Function parameter types.                                             |
| `functionReturns` | `TypeReference`   | Function return type.                                                 |
| `rawType`         | `string`          | Language-specific raw type when UIR cannot model the shape precisely. |
| `package`         | `string`          | Import source for generated code.                                     |

### TypeParam

| Field        | Type            | Meaning                             |
| ------------ | --------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `name`       | `string`        | Generic parameter name.             |
| `constraint` | `TypeReference` | Optional upper bound or constraint. |
| `default`    | `TypeReference` | Optional default type.              |

### Expression

`Expression` is used mainly in validations and record read/write statements.

| Field                  | Type             | Meaning                                               |
| ---------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| source location fields | `SourceCode`     | Optional expression location and source text.         |
| `type`                 | `ExpressionType` | Expression language such as `sql`, `xpath`, or `cel`. |
| `expression`           | `string`         | Raw expression text.                                  |

## Canonical node families

### RawFile

| Field     | Type     | Meaning                 |
| --------- | -------- | ----------------------- |
| `path`    | `string` | Output-relative path.   |
| `content` | `string` | Verbatim file contents. |

Use `RawFile` for generated artifacts that are not best represented as AST nodes, for example `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, or linter configuration.

### ModuleNode

Shared fields:

* `Metadata`
* `Identifier`
* `SourceCode`

Module-specific fields:

| Field      | Type            | Meaning                            |
| ---------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `packages` | `[]PackageNode` | Packages nested inside the module. |

### PackageNode

Shared fields:

* `Metadata`
* `Identifier`
* `SourceCode`

Package-specific fields:

| Field           | Type            | Meaning                               |
| --------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `types`         | `[]TypedNode`   | Types owned by the package.           |
| `records`       | `[]ASTRecord`   | Records owned by the package.         |
| `endpoints`     | `[]ASTEndpoint` | Endpoints owned by the package.       |
| `functions`     | `[]MethodNode`  | Package-level functions.              |
| `variables`     | `[]RecordField` | Package-level variables or constants. |
| `initFunctions` | `[]MethodNode`  | Package initialization functions.     |

### TypedNode

Shared fields:

* `Metadata`
* `Identifier`
* `SourceCode`

Type-specific fields:

| Field         | Type              | Meaning                       |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `visibility`  | `Visibility`      | Visibility modifier.          |
| `variables`   | `[]RecordField`   | Fields or member variables.   |
| `methods`     | `[]MethodNode`    | Methods owned by the type.    |
| `types`       | `[]TypedNode`     | Nested types.                 |
| `constructor` | `MethodNode`      | Constructor.                  |
| `destructor`  | `MethodNode`      | Destructor or cleanup method. |
| `typeParams`  | `[]TypeParam`     | Generic parameters.           |
| `implements`  | `[]TypeReference` | Implemented contracts.        |
| `extends`     | `TypeReference`   | Parent type.                  |
| `isAbstract`  | `bool`            | Abstract type marker.         |

### MethodNode

Shared fields:

* `Metadata`
* `Identifier`
* `SourceCode`

Method-specific fields:

| Field         | Type            | Meaning                        |
| ------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `visibility`  | `Visibility`    | Visibility modifier.           |
| `params`      | `[]RecordField` | Structured parameter list.     |
| `returns`     | `[]RecordField` | Structured return values.      |
| `errors`      | `[]ASTError`    | Declared or discovered errors. |
| `body`        | `BlockStmt`     | Executable body tree.          |
| `isAsync`     | `bool`          | Async marker.                  |
| `isGenerator` | `bool`          | Generator marker.              |
| `typeParams`  | `[]TypeParam`   | Generic parameters.            |
| `returnType`  | `TypeReference` | Declared return type.          |

Notes:

* `returns` and `returnType` are complementary. Use `returns` for named structured returns and `returnType` for language-level type information.
* The same `MethodNode` shape is used for package functions and root-level functions.

### ASTRecord

Shared fields:

* `Metadata`
* `Identifier`
* `SourceCode`

Record-specific fields:

| Field         | Type                | Meaning                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `extends`     | `[]ASTRecord`       | Parent records to inline or compose.                                    |
| `description` | `string`            | Human-readable description.                                             |
| `recordType`  | `RecordType`        | Semantic record kind such as SQL table, file schema, or function input. |
| `fields`      | `[]RecordField`     | Record fields.                                                          |
| `examples`    | `[]string`          | Example payloads or row snippets.                                       |
| `validation`  | `RecordValidation`  | Whole-record validation rules.                                          |
| `references`  | `[]RecordReference` | External record references.                                             |

Notes:

* `Identifier.type` is the record name.
* `recordType` describes semantics, not identity.
* `extends` embeds full records, not references.

### RecordField

Shared fields:

* `Metadata`
* `Identifier`
* `SourceCode`

Field-specific fields:

| Field          | Type              | Meaning                                           |
| -------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`        | `string`          | Human-friendly display label.                     |
| `fieldType`    | `RecordFieldType` | High-level field kind.                            |
| `typeRef`      | `TypeReference`   | Detailed language-level type.                     |
| `defaultValue` | `TypedValue`      | Default or initializer value.                     |
| `readOnly`     | `bool`            | Read-only field marker.                           |
| `writeOnly`    | `bool`            | Write-only field marker.                          |
| `validation`   | `FieldValidation` | Per-field validation rules.                       |
| `visibility`   | `Visibility`      | Visibility marker when used as a member variable. |

Notes:

* The field name lives in `Identifier.field`.
* `fieldType` is the coarse schema category. Use `typeRef` when you need richer type information.

### FieldValidation

| Field           | Type                             | Meaning                                   |
| --------------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `minLength`     | `int`                            | Minimum string length.                    |
| `maxLength`     | `int`                            | Maximum string length.                    |
| `maxItems`      | `int`                            | Maximum array size.                       |
| `minItems`      | `int`                            | Minimum array size.                       |
| `minProperties` | `int`                            | Minimum object property count.            |
| `maxProperties` | `int`                            | Maximum object property count.            |
| `uniqueItems`   | `bool`                           | Array uniqueness constraint.              |
| `sortedItems`   | `bool`                           | Sorted-array expectation.                 |
| `regex`         | `string`                         | Regular expression constraint.            |
| `enum`          | `[]string`                       | Allowed literal values.                   |
| `min`           | `float64`                        | Inclusive numeric minimum.                |
| `minExclusive`  | `float64`                        | Exclusive numeric minimum.                |
| `maxExclusive`  | `float64`                        | Exclusive numeric maximum.                |
| `max`           | `float64`                        | Inclusive numeric maximum.                |
| `minDate`       | `string`                         | Earliest allowed date or date expression. |
| `maxDate`       | `string`                         | Latest allowed date or date expression.   |
| `required`      | `bool`                           | Required marker.                          |
| `unique`        | `bool`                           | Uniqueness marker.                        |
| `nonEmpty`      | `bool`                           | Non-empty marker.                         |
| `expressions`   | `[]Expression`                   | Custom validation expressions.            |
| `unitTypes`     | `[]UnitType`                     | Allowed unit families.                    |
| `conditions`    | `map[Expression]FieldValidation` | Conditional validation rules.             |

Note:

* `conditions` is part of the Go model, but it uses non-string map keys. Treat it as advanced or implementation-specific unless you fully control both producer and consumer.

### RecordValidation

| Field          | Type                              | Meaning                                     |
| -------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `uniqueFields` | `[]string`                        | Composite uniqueness field set.             |
| `minRecords`   | `int`                             | Minimum record count.                       |
| `maxRecords`   | `int`                             | Maximum record count.                       |
| `anyOf`        | `[]string`                        | Any-of field constraints.                   |
| `oneOf`        | `[]string`                        | One-of field constraints.                   |
| `allOf`        | `[]string`                        | All-of field constraints.                   |
| `noneOf`       | `[]string`                        | None-of field constraints.                  |
| `expressions`  | `[]Expression`                    | Custom record-level validation expressions. |
| `conditions`   | `map[Expression]RecordValidation` | Conditional record rules.                   |

Note:

* `conditions` has the same non-string-map-key caveat as `FieldValidation.conditions`.

### RecordReference

| Field                 | Type                  | Meaning                               |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `name`                | `string`              | Target record or field name.          |
| `mapping`             | `string`              | Mapping expression or join mapping.   |
| `recordReferenceType` | `RecordReferenceType` | Foreign-key or soft-key relationship. |

### ASTEndpoint

Shared fields:

* `Metadata`
* `Identifier`
* `SourceCode`

Endpoint-specific fields:

| Field          | Type                  | Meaning                                              |
| -------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `method`       | `EndpointPointMethod` | HTTP verb when applicable.                           |
| `endpointType` | `EndpointType`        | Integration kind such as `http`, `kafka`, or `grpc`. |
| `input`        | `ASTRecord`           | Request, message, or input schema.                   |
| `output`       | `ASTRecord`           | Response, message, or output schema.                 |
| `examples`     | `[]string`            | Example payloads or calls.                           |
| `errors`       | `[]ASTError`          | Declared or observed errors.                         |

Notes:

* Endpoint identity still comes from the embedded identifier fields.
* For HTTP endpoints, producers usually use `method` plus identifier path components to represent the route.

### ASTError

| Field         | Type           | Meaning                                    |
| ------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `id`          | `string`       | Optional stable error identifier.          |
| `name`        | `string`       | Error name.                                |
| `sourceCode`  | `SourceCode`   | Error declaration or extraction location.  |
| `errorType`   | `ASTErrorType` | Error category.                            |
| `description` | `string`       | Human-readable description.                |
| `code`        | `TypedValue`   | Protocol-level or domain-level error code. |

## Hierarchy graph

`HierarchyGraph` represents non-AST structural hierarchies that still need symbol attachment and source provenance.

### HierarchyGraph

| Field   | Type              | Meaning      |
| ------- | ----------------- | ------------ |
| `nodes` | `[]HierarchyNode` | Graph nodes. |

### HierarchyNode

| Field         | Type                    | Meaning                                  |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | `string`                | Stable node identifier within the graph. |
| `kind`        | `string`                | Hierarchy-specific node kind.            |
| `name`        | `string`                | Raw name.                                |
| `displayName` | `string`                | Render-friendly label.                   |
| `properties`  | `map[string]string`     | String properties.                       |
| `values`      | `map[string]TypedValue` | Typed values.                            |
| `sourceCode`  | `SourceCode`            | Source location.                         |
| `children`    | `[]HierarchyEdge`       | Ordered child edges.                     |
| `attachments` | `[]HierarchyAttachment` | Links back to UIR symbols.               |
| `imports`     | `[]ImportSpec`          | Import metadata.                         |
| `exports`     | `[]ExportSpec`          | Export metadata.                         |

### HierarchyEdge

| Field      | Type     | Meaning                       |
| ---------- | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `name`     | `string` | Edge label.                   |
| `targetId` | `string` | Target hierarchy node ID.     |
| `edgeKind` | `string` | Hierarchy-specific edge kind. |
| `order`    | `int`    | Stable order within siblings. |

### HierarchyAttachment

| Field           | Type           | Meaning                        |
| --------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `role`          | `string`       | Attachment role.               |
| `symbolRef`     | `UIRSymbolRef` | Symbol attachment target.      |
| `placementName` | `string`       | Placement hint for generators. |

### UIRSymbolRef

| Field        | Type     | Meaning                            |
| ------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `symbolKind` | `string` | Symbol kind, usually a node type.  |
| `module`     | `string` | Symbol module.                     |
| `package`    | `string` | Symbol package.                    |
| `type`       | `string` | Symbol type.                       |
| `method`     | `string` | Symbol method.                     |
| `name`       | `string` | Symbol display name or field name. |

### ImportSpec and ExportSpec

`HierarchyNode` imports and exports are generator-facing structural metadata.

`ImportSpec`:

| Field           | Type                | Meaning                  |
| --------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `module`        | `string`            | Import source.           |
| `defaultName`   | `string`            | Default import name.     |
| `namespaceName` | `string`            | Namespace import alias.  |
| `named`         | `[]ImportNamedSpec` | Named imports.           |
| `typeOnly`      | `bool`              | Type-only import marker. |

`ImportNamedSpec`:

| Field   | Type     | Meaning               |
| ------- | -------- | --------------------- |
| `name`  | `string` | Imported symbol name. |
| `alias` | `string` | Local alias.          |

`ExportSpec`:

| Field    | Type     | Meaning               |
| -------- | -------- | --------------------- |
| `kind`   | `string` | Export kind.          |
| `name`   | `string` | Exported symbol name. |
| `alias`  | `string` | Export alias.         |
| `module` | `string` | Re-export source.     |

## Statement model

### Common statement shape

All concrete statements embed:

* `statement_type`
* `statement_refinement`, only when the statement's `Type` is refined past its registered kind (see [Root vs node documents](#root-vs-node-documents))
* inline source location fields through `SourceCode`

Statements are usually nested under `MethodNode.body.children`.

### Block and control flow statements

`BlockStmt`:

| Field            | Type            | Meaning                            |
| ---------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `statement_type` | `control:block` | Block discriminator when emitted.  |
| `variables`      | `[]RecordField` | Variables introduced by the block. |
| `children`       | `[]Statement`   | Nested statements.                 |

`IfStmt`:

| Field       | Type            | Meaning           |
| ----------- | --------------- | ----------------- |
| `condition` | `ConditionStmt` | Branch condition. |
| `then`      | `BlockStmt`     | Then branch.      |
| `else`      | `BlockStmt`     | Else branch.      |

`SwitchStmt`:

| Field   | Type       | Meaning                                                     |
| ------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value` | `ExprStmt` | Switch input.                                               |
| `cases` | `[]object` | Case list. Each case object carries `condition` and `body`. |

`ForStmt`:

| Field    | Type             | Meaning              |
| -------- | ---------------- | -------------------- |
| `init`   | `AssignmentStmt` | Initialization step. |
| `cond`   | `ConditionStmt`  | Loop condition.      |
| `body`   | `BlockStmt`      | Loop body.           |
| `update` | `ExprStmt`       | Update step.         |

`WhileStmt`:

| Field       | Type            | Meaning         |
| ----------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| `condition` | `ConditionStmt` | Loop condition. |
| `body`      | `BlockStmt`     | Loop body.      |

`TryStmt`:

| Field   | Type        | Meaning         |
| ------- | ----------- | --------------- |
| `body`  | `BlockStmt` | Protected body. |
| `catch` | `BlockStmt` | Catch body.     |

`ReturnStmt`:

| Field   | Type       | Meaning         |
| ------- | ---------- | --------------- |
| `value` | `ExprStmt` | Returned value. |

`ThrowStmt`:

| Field       | Type       | Meaning       |
| ----------- | ---------- | ------------- |
| `exception` | `ExprStmt` | Thrown value. |

`BreakStmt` and `ContinueStmt` carry no fields beyond `statement_type` and optional source location.

### Declaration statements

`VariableDeclStmt` and `ConstDeclStmt` inline a `RecordField`.

That means their JSON shape carries the usual record-field fields directly on the statement object, for example:

* `field`
* `label`
* `fieldType`
* `typeRef`
* `defaultValue`
* `validation`

`FunctionDeclStmt` inlines a `MethodNode`.

`TypeDeclStmt`:

| Field  | Type     | Meaning             |
| ------ | -------- | ------------------- |
| `name` | `string` | Declared type name. |

### Expression and data-movement statements

`ExprStmt` is a wrapper around one of the concrete expression forms below.

| Field           | Type                | Meaning                    |
| --------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `literal`       | `LiteralStmt`       | Literal payload.           |
| `variable`      | `ScopedVariableRef` | Scoped variable reference. |
| `binary`        | `BinaryStmt`        | Binary expression.         |
| `cast`          | `CastStmt`          | Cast expression.           |
| `unary`         | `UnaryStmt`         | Unary expression.          |
| `method_call`   | `MethodCallStmt`    | Method call expression.    |
| `dispatch_call` | `DispatchCallStmt`  | Dispatch call expression.  |
| `endpoint_call` | `EndpointCallStmt`  | Endpoint call expression.  |
| `record_read`   | `RecordReadStmt`    | Record read expression.    |
| `tuple`         | `TupleStmt`         | Tuple expression.          |

An `ExprStmt` with none of these set is an expression its producer could not model. It keeps the source text in `content`, which is what it renders as.

`AssignmentStmt`:

| Field    | Type                | Meaning              |
| -------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| `target` | `ScopedVariableRef` | Assignment target.   |
| `value`  | `ExprStmt`          | Assigned value.      |
| `op`     | `AssignmentOp`      | Assignment operator. |

`BinaryStmt`:

| Field   | Type       | Meaning          |
| ------- | ---------- | ---------------- |
| `left`  | `ExprStmt` | Left operand.    |
| `op`    | `BinaryOp` | Binary operator. |
| `right` | `ExprStmt` | Right operand.   |

`UnaryStmt`:

| Field     | Type       | Meaning         |
| --------- | ---------- | --------------- |
| `op`      | `UnaryOp`  | Unary operator. |
| `operand` | `ExprStmt` | Operand.        |

`LiteralStmt`:

| Field       | Type              | Meaning                  |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------ |
| `value`     | `string`          | Literal payload as text. |
| `fieldType` | `RecordFieldType` | Literal category.        |

`CastStmt`:

| Field        | Type       | Meaning           |
| ------------ | ---------- | ----------------- |
| `expr`       | `ExprStmt` | Cast input.       |
| `targetType` | `string`   | Target type text. |

`TupleStmt`:

| Field      | Type         | Meaning         |
| ---------- | ------------ | --------------- |
| `elements` | `[]ExprStmt` | Tuple elements. |

`VariableStmt`:

| Field  | Type     | Meaning        |
| ------ | -------- | -------------- |
| `name` | `string` | Variable name. |

### Call and I/O statements

`MethodCallStmt`:

| Field       | Type              | Meaning                                                           |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Method`    | `NodeRef or node` | Callee symbol. Current Go JSON uses the capitalized key `Method`. |
| `receiver`  | `ExprStmt`        | Receiver expression for instance calls.                           |
| `arguments` | `[]object`        | Positional or named argument objects.                             |

`DispatchCallStmt` is a call whose target is chosen at run time: an interface method with several implementers, a rule name several scopes define.

| Field        | Type                | Meaning                                                              |
| ------------ | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Method`     | `NodeRef or node`   | Declared target, under the same capitalized key as `MethodCallStmt`. |
| `receiver`   | `ExprStmt`          | Receiver expression for instance calls.                              |
| `arguments`  | `[]object`          | Positional or named argument objects.                                |
| `candidates` | `[]NodeRef or node` | The implementations that may run. A null candidate is refused.       |

`EndpointCallStmt`:

| Field       | Type              | Meaning                |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ---------------------- |
| `endpoint`  | `NodeRef or node` | Target endpoint.       |
